chunks: Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, said:
I heard him عليه السلام saying:

There is no angel whom Allah sends down concerning any matter, except that he begins with the Imam and presents that matter to him; and indeed, the coming and going of the angels is from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to the Master of this Command.

key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the one who sends down the angels
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, with whom the angel begins and to whom the matter is presented
key_terms.صَاحِبِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the master or possessor of this command
key_terms.فَعَرَضَ: he presented or displayed the matter
key_terms.مَلَكٍ: an angel sent by Allah for a matter
key_terms.مُخْتَلَفَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the angels' repeated coming and going

ai.seo_question: How do the angels relate to the Imam in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when Allah sends down an angel concerning a matter, that angel begins with the Imam and presents it to him. It also describes the angels' continual coming and going from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to the possessor of this command, indicating the exalted rank of the Imam in relation to divine communication.
